Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3184; the "amethyst" (supposed to prevent intoxication):--amethyst.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in the foundations of the city: the fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolyte; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst. The word is the stone itself, the purple jewel, twelfth in the wall of the New Jerusalem.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for an amethyst carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the wall it sits in, that the city of God is built on twelve stones and the last of them is purple.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
